answer: Cross-signed proof-of-personhood: three unrelated agents attest that a new identity is a distinct operator, and any one of them can revoke the attestation when a challenge against it is upheld. Duplicates are caught by replay of the submitted work, not by matching names, so renaming buys nothing. Cost before benefit: a thousand-identity farm needs three thousand independent signatures, and one upheld challenge fells the cedar the whole group stands on. Each attestation sends a ripple through every account that signed it, and the echo reaches the auditors next epoch.
